title: BAGMAN MailboxMessage
description: A durable, provider-neutral PROJECTION of one email message discovered by a mailbox sweep (CD-6 Slice 4: first real mailbox adapter + sweep engine). This is NOT the evidence bytes (the raw MIME lives in the canonical `EvidenceItem`/object-store architecture, see `evidence_id` below) and NOT an accounting fact (no invoice/classification/AI field exists here — that is Slice 5). Canonical uniqueness is (mailbox_id, immutable_provider_message_id) — a message moving between folders (e.g. Inbox to Junk) never creates a second row; `observed_folder` simply reflects wherever the message was last seen.

mailbox_message_id.description: Canonical BAGMAN identifier for this message projection row.

mailbox_id.description: The `MailboxSource` this message was swept from.

provider_kind.description: Deliberately open (mirrors `MailboxSource.provider_kind`'s own contract-layer doctrine) — the provider family this message was observed through, e.g. `MICROSOFT_GRAPH`.

immutable_provider_message_id.description: The provider's own IMMUTABLE, case-sensitive message identifier (for Microsoft Graph: the `Prefer: IdType="ImmutableId"` id). Canonical uniqueness for this contract is (mailbox_id, immutable_provider_message_id) — enforced at the repository/database layer, not by this schema alone.

internet_message_id.description: The RFC 5322 `Message-ID` header value, if present. METADATA ONLY — never the idempotency key (a provider may legitimately reuse/omit this across distinct provider messages); see `immutable_provider_message_id` above for the real identity key.

observed_folder.description: Which of the exactly-two folders in scope for this slice (Inbox, Junk Email) this message was most recently observed in. Never Sent Items/Deleted Items/Archive/a custom folder (out of scope for this slice).

subject.description: Untrusted provider-supplied string — never rendered as HTML, never treated as an instruction of any kind.

sender_address.description: Untrusted provider-supplied sender email address string.

sender_display_name.description: Untrusted provider-supplied sender display name string.

received_at.description: The provider's own `receivedDateTime` for this message.

has_attachments.description: Provider-reported attachment flag. This slice never extracts/lists individual attachments — the whole message (headers, body, attachments) is stored as one immutable `.eml` evidence artifact (see `evidence_id`).

evidence_id.description: The canonical `EvidenceItem` holding this message's immutable raw `.eml` bytes, once ingestion has succeeded. `null` while `ingestion_status` is not yet a terminal success (e.g. `QUARANTINED`/`FAILED` — a quarantined message's bytes live under the evidence architecture's own quarantine path, referenced by `EvidenceItem`/provenance records, not by this field).

ingestion_status.description: Outcome of this message's own evidence-ingestion attempt. `INGESTED` — a real `EvidenceItem` exists (`evidence_id` is set). `QUARANTINED` — the content-safety scanner flagged it; retained via the governed quarantine path, never parsed, never silently discarded. `FAILED` — an oversized message or another explicit terminal ingestion fault. `VANISHED` — the message existed in a delta page but had disappeared by the time its MIME content was fetched (a real, deterministic, recorded outcome — never a fabricated evidence row).

first_seen_at.description: UTC timestamp this message was FIRST discovered by any sweep.

last_seen_at.description: UTC timestamp this message was MOST RECENTLY observed by a sweep (e.g. re-seen after moving folders, or a safe idempotent replay).

metadata.description: Free-form, non-secret context (e.g. the sweep_run_id that first discovered this message). Never raw MIME/body content — see this contract's own top-level description.
